chapter_title: Also concerning the Catechumen; shall he be saved in a single Body?
chapter_note: This chapter contains no identifiable cosmological-correspondential substrate. It is entirely composed of institutional material about catechumenate practices (fasting rules, alms, prayer schedules, sin-accounting, forgiveness conditions), wrapped in dialogue frame and closed with exhortation. Teaching purity is 0.055 — near zero. Cosmological vocabulary appears sporadically ('light from darkness,' 'Light Mind,' 'light image,' 'land of rest') but always in service of institutional soteriology, never as systematic cosmos-to-cosmos mapping. The NT citation of 1 Cor. 7 in ¶4 is explicitly flagged as a Gospel-derived teaching. The chapter is a pure product of the Manichaean institutional layer — prescriptive rules for the catechumenate with eschatological incentives.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic disciple question opening. 'Firmaments above' and 'place of rest' are cosmological destinations but function here as endpoints of an institutional soteriology question, not systematic cosmic mapping.

Continuation of disciple question with honorific ('I beseech you, my master') and institutional content ('works of that catechumen,' 'proclaim it to the catechumens'). The questions about 'archetype' and 'sign' are institutional markers, not cosmological structure.

Dialogue frame opening ('Then the apostle says to him') followed by institutional teaching about the perfect catechumen's lifestyle — wife as stranger, house as lodging, possessions as borrowed vessels, heart on the holy church. Metaphors describe moral comportment, not cosmic correspondences. Gold/silver/utensils here are literal worldly possessions, not metal-body mappings.

Continues institutional teaching. Contains explicit NT citation (1 Cor. 7:29-31) flagged by the text itself: 'what [the] saviour put in the mouth of his apostle.' This is a 3rd-century editorial act citing Paul through Mani. 'Elect men and women' is institutional vocabulary.
Summary statement about perfect catechumens. 'They are like the elect in their constitution' — institutional comparison. High institutional score (17.78).

Seam flag fires correctly — this extends the institutional teaching with more catechumenate behavioral prescriptions: fasting, prayer, alms, church attendance, stripping worldly things. Heavy institutional vocabulary (15.2). 'The Mind that is in the holy church' uses cosmological term 'Mind' in institutional context.

Institutional summary. References Mani's own text ('Treasure of Life') — a biographical/institutional marker. 'Good pearl' metaphor is parabolic, not cosmological-correspondential. Highest institutional score so far (23.64).

Describes post-mortem journey of perfect catechumens. Contains cosmological imagery (purification in heavens, land of the living) but used as institutional reward structure. The alms-offering analogy ('just as... alms-offering that passes over to the elect') is institutional — it maps catechumen souls onto the alms system, not cosmos onto cosmos.
References 'Treasure of Life' again — Mani's institutional text. 'Each one of them in accordance with his deeds and his contribution to the church' — pure institutional merit-accounting.

Seam flag correctly identifies editorial extension. Bridge connective 'Therefore, because of this' introduces prescriptive institutional rule: catechumen should pray for repentance and forgiveness. Highest institutional score (27.27) to this point.

Transitional disciple response formula: 'when his disciples had heard... they praised him.' Contains beatitude ('Blessed are you, our father') but as part of dialogue frame response, not compiler-added devotional closure. References to elect commandments and catechumen steps are institutional vocabulary within the frame.

Extended disciple question. Frame formula ('we beseech you, our master') wraps a question about pre-conversion sins. Lists specific sins (idolatry, blasphemy, murder, adultery, magic, false witness) and 'the teaching of the sects' — all institutional/contemporary references, not cosmological structure. 'They even profaned the light-givers that are in the heavens' uses cosmological vocabulary in institutional context.

Dialogue frame opening ('Then the apostle says to them') followed by institutional teaching on forgiveness. 'Separated the light from the darkness' and 'mysteries of the living soul' are cosmological phrases used as institutional markers of conversion status. 'Right hand of peace from the Light Mind who dwells in the holy church' — cosmological entity (Light Mind) embedded in institutional ritual.

Institutional teaching on forgiveness of pre-conversion sins conditional on persisting in belief. 'Sects and idols of error' — contemporary religious landscape. Conditional structure ('if he may persist... if he shall not sin') is prescriptive institutional language.

Warning about apostasy with institutional consequence framework. Seam flag fires. Heavy institutional vocabulary: repentance, forgiveness, catechumenate, elect state, catechumen. Entirely prescriptive-institutional.
Brief institutional rule. Highest institutional score in chapter (52.78). Pure catechumenate prescriptive content: fasting, prayer, alms as sin-absolving practices.

Detailed prescriptive institutional content: fifty fasts, lord's days, sexual purification rules, dietary restrictions (no fish, no flesh/blood). 'Living soul' is cosmological vocabulary used in institutional dietary prohibition context. Very specific institutional calendar (fifty lord's days of the year).

Institutional merit-accounting system: prayer hours, daily alms, fasting, clothing the saints, 'daily communion.' Calculates that half the catechumen's work goes to good, half to sins. Pure institutional bookkeeping.

Continues institutional sin-accounting: sins divided into five parts, four absolved by church protection and faith. 'Separated the light from the darkness' again used as institutional marker. 'Holy church' and 'elect' as institutional agents of absolution.

Highest substrate score (8.97) but institutional=0.0. Contains cosmological process vocabulary: 'purified above or below,' 'cleansed and washed and adorned,' 'sculpted a light image,' 'land of rest.' These describe a genuine cosmic process but function here as the reward endpoint of the institutional sin-accounting system (the 'single part' remaining from ¶19). Final phrase echoes Matt. 6:21. Uncertain whether purification language preserves an older teaching fragment — but as positioned, it serves the institutional argument.
Brief institutional summary conditional. 'Steadfast in his catechumenate' — pure institutional vocabulary (40.0 score).

Warning about apostasy. No institutional vocabulary (0.0) but content is part of the institutional consequence structure — sins recounted, judgement poured. General moral-judicial language rather than cosmological mapping.

Devotional closure with eschatological promise: 'saves his life in the life for ever and ever,' 'rest in the life for ever.' Exhortation score 19.67. Classic compiler-added reward promise appended to institutional teaching sequence.

Closing dialogue frame formula: 'When these disciples had heard these lessons of wisdom, they gave glory to their teacher.' The phrase 'the first light, the one that brings understanding through the Mind' uses cosmological vocabulary in devotional/formulaic context, not systematic mapping.
